[M157] [Actor] Observe target surface when WaitTool fails safety checks

Original change's description:
> [Actor] Observe target surface when WaitTool fails safety checks
>
> This CL tries to solve an issue that when calling WaitTool on an empty
> tab, although the action result is correct(kUrlBlocked), it include no
> tabs.
>
> The issue is caused by that when a ToolRequest with a null
> ActorSurfaceHandle fails pre-execution checks in
> ExecutionEngine::KickOffNextAction() or
> ExecutionEngine::DidFinishAsyncSafetyChecks(), ToolController is never
> reached and WaitTool::UpdateTaskBeforeInvoke() does not run. When no
> other tabs have been added to the ActorTask yet, this leaves both
> controlled_tabs_ and to_observe_tabs_ empty, causing
> BuildActionsResultWithObservations() to return an ActionsResult with no
> TabObservation.
>
> Changes:
> - Check GetActorSurfaceForValidation() for crashed renderers in
>   ExecutionEngine::KickOffNextAction(), and call
>   ObserveActorSurfaceOnce() in KickOffNextAction() and
>   DidFinishAsyncSafetyChecks() when GetActorSurfaceHandle() is
>   null.
> - Update WaitTool::UpdateTaskBeforeInvoke() to call
>   ObserveActorSurfaceOnce() directly.
> - Verify in WaitTool_DontRecordActOnTask and
>   WaitTool_BlockedByScheme that the observed tab is recorded in
>   GetLastActedTabs() without adding it to GetTabs().
>

[M157] Allow calls to GetAssociatedRFHType() for CANCELING navs

Original change's description:
> Allow calls to GetAssociatedRFHType() for CANCELING navs
>
> When a NavigationThrottle cancels a navigation (e.g. due to the
> URLBlocklist policy or mixed content), the NavigationRequest moves to
> CANCELING but isn't deleted synchronously (OnStartChecksComplete()
> posts a task to OnRequestFailedInternal()). If another pending commit
> navigation in the same frame gets its NavigationClient disconnected in
> the meantime, DiscardSpeculativeRFHIfUnused() calls
> GetAssociatedRFHType() on the CANCELING request and hits a CHECK,
> crashing the browser.
>
> This is safe to allow: the CHECK guards against `associated_rfh_type_`
> going stale after a navigation moves to its final RenderFrameHost
> (READY_TO_COMMIT and later). Unlike the pending commit navigation
> above, the canceled navigation in CANCELING hasn't reached that point
> and is still owned by the FrameTreeNode, so its `associated_rfh_type_`
> is as accurate as for WILL_FAIL_REQUEST, which is already allowed. It
> also gives the right answer to DiscardSpeculativeRFHIfUnused(): a
> speculative RenderFrameHost still associated with the canceled
> navigation is kept rather than discarded.
>
> This is a long-standing crash and a top fatal browser crash on
> ChromeOS stable, frequently hit by enterprises using URLBlocklist
> policies.
>

[M157] Exclude Xiaomi devices from top-resumed activity focus tracking in Omnibox

Original change's description:
> Exclude Xiaomi devices from top-resumed activity focus tracking in Omnibox
>
> Users on Xiaomi devices running Android 17 (HyperOS 3/4) report that
> Omnibox search suggestions and the zero-prefix Edit/Copy URL row stop
> appearing until the phone is rebooted, while rolling back to Chrome 146
> restores suggestions immediately.
>
> We hypothesize that Xiaomi's onTopResumedActivityChanged signaling is
> compromised on these builds: once the OS window manager / launcher
> enters this state, Activity.onTopResumedActivityChanged(true) is no
> longer delivered when Chrome resumes. Because AutocompleteMediator
> initializes mActivityWindowFocused from activity.hasWindowFocus() during
> Activity.onCreate() (when the window is not yet focused) and gates
> OnSuggestionsReceivedListener registration on mActivityWindowFocused,
> missing the onTopResumedActivityChanged(true) signal leaves the
> suggestions observer permanently detached and the dropdown hidden,
> resulting in no suggestions being shown to the user.
>
> Exclude Xiaomi devices from top-resumed activity focus tracking in
> AutocompleteMediator by defaulting mActivityWindowFocused to true at
> construction and ignoring onTopResumedActivityChanged callbacks.
>

[M157] [Sharing] Fix SharingService wedging in REGISTERING state

Original change's description:
> [Sharing] Fix SharingService wedging in REGISTERING state
>
> When SharingDeviceRegistrationImpl finishes retrieving the FCM token
> and encryption info, it saves LocalSharingInfo to Sync before
> invoking SharingService::OnDeviceRegistered(). If SyncService is in
> a transient state such as TransportState::CONFIGURING when
> OnDeviceRegistered(kSuccess) runs, both IsSyncEnabledForSharing()
> and IsSyncDisabledForSharing() return false, leaving SharingService
> permanently wedged in State::REGISTERING without calling
> fcm_handler_->StartListening(). Similarly, fatal registration errors
> left state_ in State::REGISTERING instead of resetting to DISABLED.
>
> Also guard against sign-out occurring while RegisterDevice() or a
> delayed retry task is in flight so late-completing registrations are
> cleaned up and stale retry tasks do not restart registration.
>
> Changes:
> - Transition to State::ACTIVE and call fcm_handler_->StartListening()
>   in SharingService::OnDeviceRegistered(kSuccess) unless
>   IsSyncDisabledForSharing() is true in
>   components/sharing_message/sharing_service.cc.
> - Check IsSyncDisabledForSharing() before State::REGISTERING on
>   kSuccess and guard RegisterDevice() and error handling against
>   sign-out races.
> - Add DeviceRegistrationWhileSyncConfiguring and
>   DeviceRegistrationFatalErrorResetsState unit tests in
>   components/sharing_message/sharing_service_unittest.cc.

[M157] views: Defer MenuRunnerImpl destruction in OnMenuClosed

MenuRunnerImpl::OnMenuClosed cleared `controller_` before invoking
ExecuteCommand and OnMenuClosed on the MenuDelegate. When a delegate
reset its MenuRunner inside those callbacks while MenuController frames
were active on the stack, MenuRunnerImpl::Release saw a null

[M157] Harden PersistentSystemProfile against corrupt segment sizes

Original change's description:
> Harden PersistentSystemProfile against corrupt segment sizes
>
> PersistentSystemProfile::RecordAllocator assumes that adopted
> system profile segments have a positive size aligned to the 4-byte
> RecordHeader boundary. If a corrupted or crafted persistent memory
> file contains a block whose size is not aligned, the remaining
> room calculation in WriteData() can underflow, resulting in an
> out-of-bounds write past the end of the segment.
>
> To prevent this:
> 1. Validate in PersistentMemoryAllocator::GetBlock() that allocated
>    blocks have a non-empty payload size aligned to kAllocAlignment.
> 2. Preserve the last valid segment reference in NextSegment() when
>    iteration reaches the end so failed allocations do not wrap
>    around to the first segment.
> 3. Verify the cached segment size in GetAsArray() calls and reset
>    pre-existing segments when constructing a writer RecordAllocator.
>

Previously, `hideFindUI` was called when displaying a new tab. However,
this was inadvertently calling `DismissFindNavigator()` on the new tab
(where Find UI is inactive) rather than the outgoing tab (where Find UI
is active) because the active WebState had already been updated to the
new tab.

https://crrev.com/c/8537589 changing `DismissFindNavigator()` to no-op
when the Find UI is inactive illustrated this issue, as the new tab
would no longer exit fullscreen mode as a side-effect. This resulted in
new test failures (crbug.com/573174179), and could potentially be seen
as a production bug as well if a user manages to change tabs with the
Find UI open.

Fix this by dismissing the Find navigator in `FindTabHelper::WasHidden`
on the outgoing WebState and removing the redundant `hideFindUI` call
from.

Original change's description:
> Reland "[glic] Fix guest screen height being 0 during warmup when initially hidden"
>
> This is a reland of commit 883c01ec6f6dc55cae1d8c93f48db2edd9955eae.
>
> PS1 is a pure reland. PS2 and PS3 fix the two test problems that caused
> the two reverts; there are no production code changes.
>
> 1) Linux MSan (revert #1, crrev.com/c/8582345):
> GlicVisibilityBrowserTest.ReloadInFloatyRendersFrame/NoWebview timed
> out. Host::Reload() synchronously destroys the old WebContents and
> immediately creates a new one; under the MSan allocator the freed slot
> is reused, so the new WebContents can be allocated at the exact same
> address as the old one. ReloadAndWait() compared raw pointers to detect
> the swap and therefore could never observe a change. Fixed by observing
> destruction of the old WebContents with content::WebContentsDestroyedWatcher
> and then waiting for the new client contents to become non-null and
> ready. (Same root cause and equivalent fix as crrev.com/c/8586976.)
>
> 2) Win11 Tests x64 (revert #2, crrev.com/c/8594620):
> All variants timed out waiting for the client WebContents to become
> VISIBLE, deterministically (24/24 on CI, 12/12 via UTR with only this
> suite on the bot). The test removed
> --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows-for-testing to get real
> occlusion tracking. On the Windows 11 browser_tests fleet the session
> is locked / display off, and NativeWindowOcclusionTrackerWin then
> reports every window as OCCLUDED regardless of geometry (see
> "If the screen is locked or off" in native_window_occlusion_tracker_win.cc).
> Diagnostics confirmed: widget visible+active, fully on a 1024x768
> display, nothing else running, WebContents visibility=OCCLUDED. Fixed by
> keeping BrowserTestBase's default switch, like every other browser_test.
> The regression this test guards (ScreenInfo / window.screen.height being
> 0 after reload or conversation switch) does not depend on OS occlusion.
>
> Also appends a short visibility-state summary (WebContents visibility,
> RWHV state, widget state, native occlusion state, display bounds) to
> the error returned by each wait helper, so a timeout on a bot shows the
> relevant state directly in the gtest failure message.
>
> Verification: win11-rel via UTR, 50 iterations per variant, 200/200
> pass; linux_chromium_msan_rel_ng via UTR, 9 iterations per variant,
